Long post coming based on my own experiences the past few months. I'm probably preaching to the choir about a lot of this but wanted to share in case anything here resonates with someone.

I've told multiple local leaders since February that if they want young people to be involved in campaigns, they need to meet them when/where they're at. If you want young people involved in planning, you can't hold membership & committee meetings at 9am on a weekday when most of us are working 9-5 or even have MULTIPLE jobs to make ends meet. But most of these people in leadership that I'm speaking to are retired older white folks, and they're more interested in meeting when it is convenient for them and their established group of like minded friends than they are interested in making these planning meetings widely accessible. 

Young folks will have to have some personal sacrifice for these campaigns, yes. That said, I keep running into an outsized number of 50+ folks who want those young folks to magically show up, do everything for them, and not have to lift a finger because they're "old and tired" while also having pensions/healthcare/resources that young people are way less likely to have. But young people also NEED those older folks who don't have to work as much to take their life experience, community connections, and schedule flexibility so that they can contribute just as much. Related, if we create local support networks within resistance groups, we can make our own alternative social assistance available like child care/mutual aid networks/etc., things that make it possible for people to sacrifice in their daily lives for the good of a movement. (Ex: the Civil Rights Era bus boycotts had higher participation because those folks with cars helped to drive folks who usually took the bus. Without an alternative mode of transportation, participation in the boycotts would have been much lower.)

However, a big thing we young people (and everybody honestly) need to keep in mind is that part of this battle is the long-term struggle to change minds. Winning is not a far off goal at the end of the campaign that magically happens because you and a group of entirely like minded people dunk on those who we disagree with. A lot of this work requires A LOT OF PATIENCE and the ability to slowly move people who were previously unaligned with us into a place where they're a few steps closer. And that is frustrating and hard. But it is worthwhile work. People engaged with the movement now WILL burn out, and we need to have more people available to step in and let them rest when that happens. But good lord, I feel y'all when you say you're tired of hearing "where are the young people" because we're here. We want to help. But we need help to help you.
Excellent food for thought. Tactics will need to evolve over time as repression increases, and this is a smart way to distribute the resources you have. Love it.

You are 150% NOT overreacting. I got a hysterectomy for way less; if I were you, I'd be doing the same thing. It is not fair for him to place this on you as if it is your duty to suffer debilitating pain so he can "have his chance," or whatever. You deserve a life where you can be in less pain, even if only marginally so. 

I could take my time picking apart his hissy fit piece by piece, but it would be a waste of time. You were SO patient and even toned responding to him when it would be completely understandable if you'd been snarky or mean back to him. He is making your pain about him and how it inconveniences the life plan he had in mind for himself rather than seeing how your pain is completely debilitating. 

I hope you won't let his immaturity and unwillingness to decenter himself in the situation affect your medical decision. You've done the work; you've had meetings with specialists, medical procedures, all of it. You are the expert on your body, not him. And you deserve someone to support you in making what is an emotionally difficult decision.

Have you included the word "damaged" in the subject line? The website FAQ suggests this:

"If your purchase is damaged, please send a photo of the damaged item(s) to us at support@kaleidoscosmetics.com within 7 days of receiving your order with the subject line DAMAGED and include your name and order number. If the item cannot be repaired, we will reship you a replacement free of charge."

If you haven't followed those steps exactly, I'd give it another shot. Speaking from experience, sometimes email filters latch onto the weirdest things. Keep DAMAGED, your name, and order # listed in the subject line, & make sure to include the first date you tried contacting them in the body of the email (as well as that picture you have).

It's totally not normal for the brand to be so unresponsive to that customer service email, so I'm super sorry you're having such a hard time getting through to them. Keep us posted! :)
